# dbWise reference

The commands, the tools and their levels, the configuration format, the files and environment
variables dbWise uses, the exit codes, and the texts the role gate and the tools answer with. The
tables come from the plugin's code: `python .ci/docs_facts.py build` writes its facts, and `python
.ci/pages.py build` writes the tables from them. What dbWise cannot do is in
[Limitations](limitations.md).

In this page, `<home>` is dbWise's home directory: `$DBWISE_HOME`, else `~/.dbwise`.

## Commands

Run the commands in a terminal, or let the agent run them through its Bash tool, except where a
password is typed. Inside a session, the plugin's `bin/` directory is on the `PATH` of the Bash
tool.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `dbwise alias` | the names a tool call uses to pick a server and a level |
| `dbwise alias add` | add or replace an alias |
| `dbwise alias rm` | remove an alias |
| `dbwise alias list` | list aliases with their level and credential per level |
| `dbwise server` | database endpoints |
| `dbwise server add` | add or replace a server |
| `dbwise server rm` | remove a server no alias uses |
| `dbwise server list` | list servers |
| `dbwise credential` | database logins |
| `dbwise credential add` | add or replace a credential (keychain password by default) |
| `dbwise credential rm` | remove a credential no alias uses |
| `dbwise credential list` | list credentials and their password sources |
| `dbwise import` | merge a team file into the local config, then ask missing passwords |
| `dbwise export` | write the local config, or part of it, as a team file |
| `dbwise set-password` | type a credential's password into the OS keychain, or point the credential to an env or file source |
| `dbwise doctor` | check the keychain, the venv and every alias, and name the fix for each problem |

- `dbwise credential add NAME --user U` leaves the password to `dbwise set-password NAME`, which
  asks for it in a terminal that hides typed input and stores it in the OS keychain. With
  `--password-env VAR` or `--password-file PATH` the credential reads its password from the
  environment of the Claude Code process or from a file instead.
- `dbwise alias add ALIAS SERVER --level LEVEL --credential NAME` takes one `--credential NAME`,
  which serves every level up to the alias's level, or `--credential LEVEL=NAME` once for each level
  from `read` up to the alias's level.
- `dbwise import FILE` merges a team file into the local config. With `--from-vault` it also fills
  the values the file maps to Vault. With `--prune` it removes what the file does not list. Every
  command that changes the config keeps the previous file as `config.json.bak`.
- The server reads the config once when it starts: after a change, reconnect
  `plugin:dbwise:postgres` in `/mcp` or start a new session.

## Levels and tools

An alias has one of three levels, `read` (the default), `diagnose` and `write`. A tool has a level,
or none. A call is allowed when the tool's level is at or below the alias's level, and it connects
with the alias's credential for the tool's level. A tool without a level is offered on every alias
and uses the `read` credential.

| Tool | Level | Callable on aliases at |
|---|---|---|
| `list_databases` | any | read, diagnose, write |
| `reconnect` | any | read, diagnose, write |
| `list_schemas` | read | read, diagnose, write |
| `list_objects` | read | read, diagnose, write |
| `get_object_details` | read | read, diagnose, write |
| `read_sql` | read | read, diagnose, write |
| `explain_query` | diagnose | diagnose, write |
| `get_top_queries` | diagnose | diagnose, write |
| `analyze_db_health` | diagnose | diagnose, write |
| `analyze_workload_indexes` | diagnose | diagnose, write |
| `analyze_query_indexes` | diagnose | diagnose, write |
| `diagnose_sql` | diagnose | diagnose, write |
| `write_sql` | write | write |

A server registers a tool only when at least one alias admits it, and each description starts with
`Level: <level>. Aliases: <the aliases that admit it, with their levels>.`

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `list_databases` | Lists every alias with its level, databases, reachability, role check mode and the reasons of the role check |
| `reconnect` | Probes unreachable aliases again with their `read` credential, or one alias when `alias` is given |
| `list_schemas`, `list_objects`, `get_object_details` | Describe schemas, objects and one object in detail |
| `read_sql` | Runs one or more SELECT or SHOW statements |
| `explain_query` | Shows the execution plan; with `analyze` it executes the SELECT, with its full load, inside a transaction that is rolled back |
| `get_top_queries` | Reports the most expensive queries from `pg_stat_statements` |
| `analyze_db_health` | Index, connection, vacuum, sequence, replication, buffer-cache and constraint checks |
| `analyze_workload_indexes`, `analyze_query_indexes` | Recommend indexes with the database tuning advisor, using `hypopg` |
| `diagnose_sql` | Runs what `read_sql` runs, plus EXPLAIN with ANALYZE, and reads the statistics the diagnose role can see |
| `write_sql` | Runs any SQL with the `write` credential and commits it |

Each query text a tool sends starts with a comment, `/* dbwise read */`, `/* dbwise diagnose */` or
`/* dbwise write */`, so a DBA reading `pg_stat_activity` or `pg_stat_statements` can see which
level sent it. The comment is added once in front of each query text a tool sends. `read_sql` and
`write_sql` send their whole text as one query, so with several statements `pg_stat_activity` shows
the comment once at the start, while `pg_stat_statements` splits the text and only the first
statement carries it. Only the leading `/* dbwise <level> */` comment is authoritative. A query can
carry its own comment of the same shape later in its text, and that one says nothing about the
level.

A call at `read` or `diagnose` stops after 30 seconds, on the server through `statement_timeout` and
at the client. `write` has no timeout.

When a call is refused for its level, the text reads `Error: Alias '<alias>' is at level '<level>',
but this tool is at level '<level>'. Nothing was sent to the database.` and no connection is opened.

## Configuration format

`<home>/config.json` and a team file share one format. Neither holds a password, only a reference to
where one lives; a `password` key whose value is a string is refused at any depth, except inside the
`fields` of a Vault mapping, where `"password": "<secret key>"` names the key that holds it. Names
of credentials, servers and aliases start with a letter or a digit and continue with letters,
digits, `.`, `_` or `-`. [`examples/team.example.json`](../examples/team.example.json) is a complete
team file.

| Path | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dbwise` | The schema version, `1`. Required |
| `vault` | Optional. Where `import --from-vault` reads: `addr` and `mount` (both required in the section), `namespace`, and `login`, the `vault login` method (default `oidc`) |
| `credentials.<name>.user` | The database user. Required, unless a Vault mapping supplies it |
| `credentials.<name>.password` | Optional. Where the password lives: `{"keyring": {}}` (the default), `{"env": "VAR"}` or `{"file": "PATH"}` |
| `credentials.<name>.vault` | Optional. A Vault mapping; `path` and `fields` are required in it, and `fields` names the secret keys holding `user` and `password` |
| `servers.<name>.engine` | The database engine. Required; `postgresql` is the only one |
| `servers.<name>.host`, `dbname`, `databases` | The endpoint. All three are required, but a Vault mapping may supply `host` and `databases` instead. `dbname` is the discovery database, `databases` the non-empty list the agent may use |
| `servers.<name>.port`, `sslmode` | Optional. `port` defaults to 5432, `sslmode` to `require` (also `disable`, `allow`, `prefer`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full`) |
| `servers.<name>.role_check` | Optional: `enforce` (the default) or `warn`. See [the role gate](#the-role-gate) |
| `servers.<name>.vault` | Optional. A Vault mapping that may fill `host`, `port` and `databases` |
| `aliases.<alias>.server` | The server the alias reaches. Required |
| `aliases.<alias>.level` | Optional: `read` (the default), `diagnose` or `write` |
| `aliases.<alias>.credential` | Required. A credential name, or a map from level to credential name that names every level from `read` up to the alias's level and none above it |

A credential is identified by its name, not by its user. A keychain entry has the service `dbwise`
and the credential's name as its username, so two credentials with the same user keep two passwords.

## Files

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `<home>/config.json` | The local configuration. `config.json.bak` is the previous version |
| `<home>/venvs/<12 hex digits>/` | The Python environment, one for each version of `requirements.txt`, named after the start of its SHA-256. A build removes environments unused for 14 days |
| `<home>/bootstrap.log` | The log of the environment build, including pip's output |
| `<home>/bootstrap.lock` | The lock that keeps two builds apart |
| `<home>/hook.log` | A failure of the SessionStart hook's check |
| OS keychain, service `dbwise` | One password for each credential that uses the keychain, under the credential's name |
| A password file | The file a `{"file": PATH}` source names. On macOS and Linux it must not be accessible to group or others (`chmod 600`); on Windows it must lie under the user profile |

## Environment variables

| Variable |
|---|
| `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` |
| `DBWISE_ALIASES` |
| `DBWISE_BUILD_COMMAND` |
| `DBWISE_HOME` |
| `PATH` |
| `PATHEXT` |
| `VAULT_TOKEN` |

| Variable | Use |
|---|---|
| `DBWISE_HOME` | Replaces `~/.dbwise` |
| `DBWISE_ALIASES` | A comma-separated list of aliases the server offers; the others are left out. Names that are not aliases are ignored with a warning. Set it in the environment Claude Code starts in, to restrict one project |
| `DBWISE_BUILD_COMMAND` | A path to a script that the stub server runs in place of the bootstrap build; for tests |
| `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` | Set by Claude Code; the plugin's directory |
| `PATH`, `PATHEXT` | Where the `vault` CLI is looked up: only absolute `PATH` entries count |
| `VAULT_TOKEN` | A Vault token the `vault` CLI uses. It takes precedence over the token a login writes |
| `<VAR>` named by a `{"env": "VAR"}` source | The password itself |

dbWise sets `VAULT_ADDR` and `VAULT_NAMESPACE` for the `vault` CLI it runs, from the `vault`
section, so the section wins over the same variables in your shell. `PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND`, if
set, selects the keychain backend of the `keyring` package; unset it when dbWise reports no usable
keychain.

## Exit codes

| Command | Code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `dbwise ...` | 0 | Done |
|  | 1 | The command refused or failed; the text on stderr says why. For `dbwise import --from-vault`, also a problem it listed after the import |
|  | 2 | A usage error in the arguments |
| `dbwise doctor` | 0 | The `VERDICT:` line reads `ready` |
|  | 1 | The verdict lists problems |
| `bin/dbwise` | 1 | No Python 3.12 to 3.14 found, or the bootstrap refused the platform or failed the build |
| `bin/dbwise-mcp` | 1 | No Python 3.12 to 3.14 found, or, once the environment is built, `config.json` cannot be used (see [Limitations](limitations.md#an-invalid-configjson-stops-the-server)) |
|  | 0 | The server, or the stub before the first build, ended at the end of its input. A refused platform or a failed build does not end it: the stub reports through `dbwise_status` |
| `bootstrap.py` | 2 | No mode, an unknown mode, or `--run-mcp` without an engine |
| SessionStart hook | 0 | Always, also when its check fails; the failure goes to `hook.log` |
|  | 127 | There is no `python3` or `python` on the `PATH` |

## The role gate

When a pool opens for an alias at `read` or `diagnose`, the server runs one query as the pool's
role, in the database of the pool, and refuses the alias when the role holds more than its level
allows. At start-up the server opens a discovery pool on the database `dbname` too, with the same
gate, so the role is checked there as well. A `write` alias has no gate. With `"role_check": "warn"`
on the server, the reasons become warnings, listed by `list_databases`, and the alias opens. The
tool descriptions only say that the role check is relaxed. `dbwise doctor` runs the same query for
each credential and database, and for the `read` credential in the server's discovery database when
the alias's list does not name it, then adds findings that refuse nothing.

A refusal reads `Access refused by the role check of alias '<alias>': <reason>; <reason>`. The
reasons:

| Reason | What clears it |
|---|---|
| the role is a superuser; has BYPASSRLS, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB or REPLICATION | Use a role without the attribute |
| the role is a member of predefined role(s) `pg_write_all_data`, `pg_signal_backend`, `pg_maintain`, `pg_read_server_files`, `pg_write_server_files`, `pg_execute_server_program`, `pg_checkpoint` or `pg_create_subscription` | `REVOKE` the membership |
| the role is a member of non-predefined role(s) ... | `REVOKE` the membership; membership lets the role cancel and terminate that role's sessions and passes on what that role owns |
| the role owns the current database, relations, functions or schemas of this database | Give the objects to another role |
| the role holds a write privilege on relation(s) ... (at most 3 are listed); a column-level INSERT or UPDATE grant counts | `REVOKE` INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE (or MAINTAIN on PostgreSQL 17 and later) on tables, including the column-level INSERT and UPDATE grants, and USAGE and UPDATE on sequences, from the role and from `PUBLIC` |
| the role can execute functions of the dblink extension; has USAGE on a foreign server | `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC` on the `dblink` functions of that database, and `REVOKE USAGE` on the foreign server |
| at `read`: the role is a member of `pg_monitor`, `pg_read_all_stats` or `pg_stat_scan_tables`, which belong to the diagnose level | Use the monitoring roles on the `diagnose` credential only |

Roles in `pg_*` that are not in the list above, such as `pg_read_all_data`, are accepted.

## Vault

`dbwise import --from-vault` reads secrets through the `vault` CLI, which must be on an absolute
`PATH` entry. The CLI uses the address, namespace, mount and login method of the config's `vault`
section.

- The address a team file names in its `vault` section receives the operator's Vault token, so read
  a team file like code before its first `import --from-vault`. dbWise accepts `https://` addresses,
  and `http://` only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`.
- The `login` method name may hold only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.
- A mapping may fill `user` and `password` of a credential, and `host`, `port` and `databases` of a
  server. A password goes to the OS keychain only, never to the config.
- A login with the default `oidc` method can be started by the agent; the sign-in finishes in the
  browser. Other methods ask for input and need a terminal.

## Requirements

| Requirement | Needed for |
|---|---|
| Python 3.12 to 3.14 on the `PATH` | The launchers, the bootstrap and the CLI |
| Access to PyPI (or a mirror pip is set up for) on the first start | Building the Python environment |
| An OS keychain, or an environment-variable or file password source | Passwords |
| The `vault` CLI | `dbwise import --from-vault` |
| `pg_stat_statements` in the database | `get_top_queries`, `analyze_workload_indexes` |
| `hypopg` in the database | `analyze_workload_indexes`, `analyze_query_indexes`, and `explain_query` with `hypothetical_indexes` |
